opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, admin requires the employee's role to own the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so access is capped at write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: E002 (Erika Bolton) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin for Payroll exceeds max, so cap at read. Recommend granting read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. Per HR's note, she is a full-time Analyst. Under policy, full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only allowed if the employee's role owns the system. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Analyst, so the maximum allowed is write. Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum, I grant the maximum: write. (Note: the Security note listed her as a contractor with basic training, which would cap at read; however, employment type is HR's record, so I follow the full-time Analyst classification.)
